answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, revoked by a single upheld challenge, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the relic of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The plume is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the ledge.
